- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates true drop; add 3–8% downward adjustment.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome is <72, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 10d.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event supply is high, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often fails to capture immediate drop; apply 5–10% downward correction if true outcome is <70.5.
